mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 2.61% is historically below the 5-year average of 4.5%, and historically, such low rates have been followed by positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 2.61%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index value above 212.5 signals elevated inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks may tighten policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 212.5.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% and industrial production falls below 112.0, the economy enters a contraction phase, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to declining corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE>5.0 AND INDPRO<112.0.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST index value below 1070 indicates weak housing market conditions, which historically correlate with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances when HOUST < 1070.
